title: Bidirectional BFS: Double-Ended Dublin Routes!
description: See how Bidirectional BFS finds the shortest path by expanding search frontiers from both start and goal simultaneously. Watch the wavefronts meet over a grid-like street graph inspired by Dublin’s Docklands layout.
ig_caption:
🚦✨ Bidirectional BFS in Dublin (Docklands)! ✨🚦

Instead of searching outward from just one point, Bidirectional BFS launches two BFS processes—one from the start node and one from the destination—until the frontiers intersect. In graph-theory terms, this reduces explored nodes by turning a single-source shortest-path search on an unweighted street graph into a meet-in-the-middle strategy, often shrinking the effective branching depth from b^d to about 2·b^(d/2). 🧠🌍

We model nearby streets as a graph (intersections = nodes, street segments = edges) and visualize the expanding layers like a ripple effect across a real-map-inspired layout. When the forward and backward searches touch, we reconstruct the shortest route with optimality guaranteed for unweighted graphs. ✅📍

fb_caption:
🚍🏙️ Dublin (Docklands) + Bidirectional BFS = smarter shortest paths!

Graph search finds routes by exploring connected nodes, and Bidirectional BFS improves the classic BFS by expanding from both the start and the goal at the same time. The moment the two search frontiers meet, we can assemble the shortest path—fast, optimal (for unweighted maps), and perfect for visual learning.
